channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Rashod Bateman (groin) was a full participant for Thursday’s practice.
item.description: Bateman got a limited practice tag Wednesday, but appears to be just fine for the Week 12 matchup against the Texans. He’s still off the fantasy radar in the majority of formats for that contest.- Christopher Crawford

item.title: Derrick Henry (concussion) was listed as a full participant for Thursday’s practice.
item.description: It’s excellent news for fantasy managers and for Henry, as he’s exited the concussion protocol. The 32-year-old should be ready to go for Week 12 against the Texans, assuming there are no setbacks.- Christopher Crawford

item.title: Darren Waller (knee) was a limited participant in Thursday’s practice.
item.description: Waller got in a limited session, as was Tommy Tremble with his own knee ailment. Mitchell Evans was not able to practice due to his Achilles injury, so the Carolina room could be in a bit of trouble for Week 12 against the Bucs.- Christopher Crawford

item.title: Jonathon Brooks (groin) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description: Brooks has a chance to face the Buccaneers this week, though Panthers coach Dave Canales acknowledged earlier this week that it will be tough to find a spot on the roster for him, due to special teams needs. Brooks is only a bench stash at this point.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Tetairoa McMillan (foot) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description: McMillan was unable to participate in today’s walkthrough, which is a bad sign for his Week 12 availability. Jalen Coker would step into No. 1 wide receiver duties if McMillan cannot play this weekend against the Buccaneers.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Omar Cooper (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description: Cooper is firmly on the wrong side of questionable for the Jets’ Week 12 game against the Dolphins. Isaiah Williams (ribs) is on track to return for No. 3 wide receiver duties, though only Garrett Wilson is reliable.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Isaiah Williams (ribs) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description: Williams should be good to go for No. 3 wide receiver duties this week. The Jets’ wide receiver corps is a little too crowded for Williams to be a serious FLEX option against the Dolphins this week, though.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Carson Beck (back) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description: Beck is unlikely to recover in time to face the Commanders on Sunday. Journeyman in-season signee Josh Johnson will likely start. Johnson will be a low-end QB2 in this instance. The team brought back Kedon Slovis via waivers this week.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Romeo Doubs (shoulder) was limited on Thursday.
item.description: Doubs has a chance to return this week, in time to face the Chargers, but he is still in the questionable column. If he upgrades tomorrow, he should be good to go. Doubs would theoretically be the Patriots’ No. 1 wide receiver, but this situation is shaky. He can be stashed in 12-team leagues.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Bhayshul Tuten (foot/ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description: Tuten aggravates his ankle and foot issues in Week 11 against the Giants. He has been playing through the ailments for multiple weeks, and still has a chance to face the Titans this week. He is an RB1 if active. Chris Rodriguez (hand) should be rostered just in case.-Nic Bodiford
